name: Web app with accounts and records (split storage)
summary: A running web app: landing page, sign up, log in, and a private dashboard where each account keeps its own records. One file to run, no build step. Storage is split into three focused modules behind a facade, to test whether smaller pieces build more reliably.
what_you_get: Four working pages: landing, sign up, log in, dashboard
Accounts with hashed passwords and real session tokens
Records that belong to one account and are invisible to every other
A REST API underneath, so the same data is reachable programmatically
guarantees: Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2 and are not recoverable from the database
Every input has a label and every control is at least 44px tall
User text is escaped, proven by storing a hostile payload and rendering it
Anonymous requests get 401 and malformed ones get 422, never a 500
One account cannot read or delete another account's records

pieces.name: passwords
pieces.spec:
Write a module with exactly two functions and no framework imports:
    hash_password(password: str) -> str
    verify_password(password: str, stored: str) -> bool

Use hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with sha256, 200000 iterations, and a random 16-byte salt from the
secrets module. hash_password returns ONE string containing the algorithm name, the iteration
count, the salt as hex and the digest as hex, separated by '$'.

verify_password must split that string into EXACTLY the same number of parts that
hash_password produced. If the two disagree, split() raises, your except clause returns False,
and every single verification fails including correct passwords. Count them.

Compare with hmac.compare_digest. Return False (never raise) for malformed, empty or None
input.
pieces.tests:
# --- blueprint scenario: exercised the way api.py actually calls it -------------
_h = hash_password("correct horse battery")
assert isinstance(_h, str) and _h, (
    "hash_password must RETURN the stored string. Got %r. api.py does "
    "storage.create_user(email, hash_password(pw)) - it stores the return value." % (_h,))
assert "correct horse battery" not in _h, (
    "hash_password returned something containing the plaintext password: %r. "
    "Hash it, do not encode it." % (_h,))
assert hash_password("correct horse battery") != _h, (
    "hash_password returned the same string twice for the same password, so it is "
    "unsalted. Generate a fresh random salt per call and store it inside the result.")
assert verify_password("correct horse battery", _h) is True, (
    "verify_password(password, stored) must return True for the right password. "
    "Note the argument order: plaintext first, stored hash second.")
assert verify_password("wrong password", _h) is False, (
    "verify_password must return False - not None, not raise - for a wrong password.")

pieces.name: store_users
pieces.spec:
Use only sqlite3, secrets, hashlib and time. Every function opens and closes its own connection to the SAME database file, `app.db`, in the current directory. Use `sqlite3.Row` and return dicts, never raw row tuples.

Write the accounts half of the storage layer.

Table: users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, created_at)

init_users() creates the table if it does not exist.
create_user(email, password_hash) returns the new user's id as an int, and raises ValueError if the email already exists.
get_user_by_email(email) returns a dict with keys id, email and password_hash, or None. The login route reads user['password_hash'], so that column must be selected.
pieces.tests:
import glob as _glob
import os as _os
for _f in _glob.glob("*.db") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite3"):
    try:
        _os.remove(_f)
    except OSError:
        pass
init_users()

_uid = create_user("scenario@test.io", "hashed-value-here")
assert _uid is not None, (
    "create_user must RETURN the new user's id. It returned None, so its caller has "
    "nothing to open a session with: api.py does create_session(create_user(e, h)).")
assert isinstance(_uid, int), (
    "create_user must return the id itself as an int, not %r." % (_uid,))

try:
    create_user("scenario@test.io", "other-hash")
    raise AssertionError(
        "create_user must raise ValueError on a duplicate email. It returned normally, "
        "so two accounts can share one address.")
except ValueError:
    pass

_user = get_user_by_email("scenario@test.io")
assert _user is not None, "get_user_by_email must find a user that was just created."
try:
    _hash = _user["password_hash"]
    _got_id = _user["id"]
except (TypeError, KeyError, IndexError):
    raise AssertionError(
        "get_user_by_email returned %r, which is a %s. It must return a dict the caller "
        "can read by name: {'id': ..., 'email': ..., 'password_hash': ...}. The login "
        "route reads user['password_hash'], so a row tuple or a bare id cannot work."
        % (_user, type(_user).__name__))
assert _hash == "hashed-value-here", (
    "get_user_by_email returned password_hash=%r, but the stored value was "
    "'hashed-value-here'. SELECT the real column." % (_hash,))
assert int(_got_id) == int(_uid), "get_user_by_email returned a different id."
assert get_user_by_email("nobody@test.io") is None, (
    "get_user_by_email must return None for an unknown email, not raise and not [].")

pieces.name: store_sessions
pieces.spec:
Use only sqlite3, secrets, hashlib and time. Every function opens and closes its own connection to the SAME database file, `app.db`, in the current directory. Use `sqlite3.Row` and return dicts, never raw row tuples.

Write the sessions half of the storage layer.

Table: sessions(token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at)

init_sessions() creates the table if it does not exist.
create_session(user_id) returns a fresh secrets.token_urlsafe token as a string and stores ONLY its sha256 hash, so a leaked database does not hand over live sessions.
user_id_for_token(token) returns the user's id as an int, or None for an unknown token - that is how the API answers 401 instead of crashing.
delete_session(token) invalidates it, so logging out actually logs out.
pieces.tests:
import glob as _glob
import os as _os
for _f in _glob.glob("*.db") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite3"):
    try:
        _os.remove(_f)
    except OSError:
        pass
init_sessions()

_tok = create_session(7)
assert isinstance(_tok, str) and len(_tok) >= 16, (
    "create_session must return the session token as a string of at least 16 characters. "
    "Got %r." % (_tok,))
assert _tok != create_session(7), (
    "create_session returned the same token twice, so every session is guessable from any "
    "other. Use secrets.token_urlsafe.")

_got = user_id_for_token(_tok)
assert _got is not None, "user_id_for_token must resolve a live token."
assert int(_got) == 7, (
    "user_id_for_token must return the user's id itself as an int, not a row tuple. "
    "Got %r." % (_got,))
assert user_id_for_token("not-a-real-token") is None, (
    "user_id_for_token must return None for an unknown token - that is how the API "
    "answers 401 instead of crashing.")

delete_session(_tok)
assert user_id_for_token(_tok) is None, (
    "delete_session must invalidate the token - logging out has to actually log out.")

# The guarantee is that a leaked database does not hand over live sessions, so the check
# is what the table actually contains, not what the module says it does.
import sqlite3 as _sqlite3
_live = create_session(8)
_conn = _sqlite3.connect("app.db")
_stored = str(_conn.execute("SELECT * FROM sessions").fetchall())
_conn.close()
assert _live not in _stored, (
    "the raw token is sitting in the sessions table, so anyone who reads the database can "
    "use it as a live session. Store ONLY its sha256 hash and hash the incoming token when "
    "looking it up.")
assert user_id_for_token(_live) == 8, (
    "storing the hash broke the lookup - hash the incoming token the same way before "
    "comparing.")

pieces.name: store_records
pieces.spec:
Use only sqlite3, secrets, hashlib and time. Every function opens and closes its own connection to the SAME database file, `app.db`, in the current directory. Use `sqlite3.Row` and return dicts, never raw row tuples.

Write the {{records}} half of the storage layer.

Table: {{records}}(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, {{title_field}}, {{amount_field}}, date, created_at)

init_records() creates the table if it does not exist.
add_record(user_id, {{title_field}}, {{amount_field}}, date) returns the created row as a dict whose keys are exactly id, {{title_field}}, {{amount_field}} and date. The frontend reads those exact names; any other spelling renders as "undefined" on screen.
list_records(user_id) returns a list of those dicts.
delete_record(record_id, user_id) returns True when it deleted something and False when it did not, so the API can answer 404.

list_records and delete_record MUST filter by user_id inside the SQL, so one account can never see or delete another account's rows.
pieces.tests:
import glob as _glob
import os as _os
for _f in _glob.glob("*.db") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite3"):
    try:
        _os.remove(_f)
    except OSError:
        pass
init_records()

_rec = add_record(1, "Sunrise loop", 12.5, "2026-01-01")
assert isinstance(_rec, dict) and "id" in _rec, (
    "add_record must return the created record as a dict including its new 'id'. "
    "Got %r." % (_rec,))

_rows = list_records(1)
assert isinstance(_rows, list) and len(_rows) == 1, (
    "list_records must return a list of the user's records. Got %r." % (_rows,))
try:
    _missing = [_k for _k in ("id", "title", "amount", "date") if _k not in _rows[0]]
except TypeError:
    raise AssertionError(
        "list_records returned %r, whose items are %s. Each item must be a dict with the "
        "keys id, title, amount and date - the dashboard renders fields by name, and any "
        "other shape shows up as 'undefined' on the page."
        % (_rows, type(_rows[0]).__name__))
assert not _missing, (
    "each record is missing %r. The dashboard renders these by name, so a missing key "
    "shows as 'undefined' on screen. Got keys %r." % (_missing, sorted(_rows[0])))
assert _rows[0]["title"] == "Sunrise loop", "list_records returned the wrong title."

assert list_records(2) == [], (
    "list_records returned another account's rows. Filter by user_id inside the SQL.")
assert delete_record(int(_rows[0]["id"]), 2) in (False, 0, None), (
    "delete_record must not delete another account's record.")
assert list_records(1) != [], (
    "delete_record deleted a record belonging to a different user - it is filtering on "
    "record id only. Filter on BOTH record_id and user_id.")

assert delete_record(int(_rows[0]["id"]), 1) in (True, 1), (
    "delete_record must return True when it deleted something, so the API can answer 404 "
    "when it did not.")
assert list_records(1) == [], "delete_record did not actually delete the record."
assert delete_record(9999, 1) in (False, 0), (
    "delete_record must return False for a record that does not exist.")

pieces.name: storage
pieces.spec: Re-export the three storage modules. Fixed source; not generated.
pieces.source:
"""The storage interface api.py imports, assembled from three focused modules.

Fixed rather than generated: re-exporting three modules has one correct answer and no
judgement in it, so a generation spent here would only add a way to fail.
"""
from store_records import add_record, delete_record, init_records, list_records
from store_sessions import (create_session, delete_session, init_sessions,
                            user_id_for_token)
from store_users import create_user, get_user_by_email, init_users

__all__ = [
    "init_db", "create_user", "get_user_by_email", "create_session",
    "user_id_for_token", "delete_session", "add_record", "list_records", "delete_record",
]


def init_db():
    """Create every table. The three modules share one database file."""
    init_users()
    init_sessions()
    init_records()
pieces.tests:
# --- blueprint scenario: exercised the way api.py actually calls it -------------
# Every assertion below mirrors one real call site. A module can define all nine
# signatures correctly and still be unusable, which is exactly what happened before
# this scenario existed.
import glob as _glob
import os as _os
# Whatever the module decided to call its database, not three guesses at it. Leftover rows
# make every attempt after the first fail on a duplicate email, which no amount of fixing
# the module can cure.
for _f in _glob.glob("*.db") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite3"):
    try:
        _os.remove(_f)
    except OSError:
        pass
init_db()

_uid = create_user("scenario@test.io", "hashed-value-here")
assert _uid is not None, (
    "create_user must RETURN the new user's id. It returned None, so its caller has "
    "nothing to open a session with: api.py does create_session(create_user(e, h)).")
assert isinstance(_uid, int), (
    "create_user must return the id itself as an int, not %r." % (_uid,))

try:
    create_user("scenario@test.io", "hashed-value-here")
    raise AssertionError(
        "create_user must raise ValueError on a duplicate email. It returned normally, "
        "so two accounts can share one address.")
except ValueError:
    pass

_user = get_user_by_email("scenario@test.io")
assert _user is not None, "get_user_by_email must find a user that was just created."
# Ask for the field rather than guessing which wrong shapes to exclude. A guard listing
# the bad types lets every unlisted one through as a bare TypeError, which tells the model
# what broke and never what was wanted.
try:
    _hash = _user["password_hash"]
    _got_id = _user["id"]
except (TypeError, KeyError, IndexError):
    raise AssertionError(
        "get_user_by_email returned %r, which is a %s. It must return a dict the caller "
        "can read by name: {'id': ..., 'email': ..., 'password_hash': ...}. The login "
        "route reads user['password_hash'] to check the password, so a row tuple or a "
        "bare id cannot work. Use sqlite3.Row and dict(row), and SELECT the hash column."
        % (_user, type(_user).__name__))
assert _hash == "hashed-value-here", (
    "get_user_by_email returned password_hash=%r but the stored value was "
    "'hashed-value-here'. SELECT the real column." % (_hash,))
assert int(_got_id) == int(_uid), (
    "get_user_by_email returned id=%r but create_user returned %r." % (_got_id, _uid))
assert get_user_by_email("nobody@test.io") is None, (
    "get_user_by_email must return None for an unknown email, not raise and not [].")

_tok = create_session(int(_uid))
assert isinstance(_tok, str) and len(_tok) >= 16, (
    "create_session must return the session token as a string of at least 16 "
    "characters. Got %r." % (_tok,))
assert user_id_for_token(_tok) is not None, "user_id_for_token must resolve a live token."
assert int(user_id_for_token(_tok)) == int(_uid), (
    "user_id_for_token must return the user's id itself (an int), not a row tuple. "
    "Got %r." % (user_id_for_token(_tok),))
assert user_id_for_token("not-a-real-token") is None, (
    "user_id_for_token must return None for an unknown token - that is how the API "
    "answers 401 instead of crashing.")

_rec = add_record(int(_uid), "Sunrise loop", 12.5, "2026-01-01")
assert isinstance(_rec, dict) and "id" in _rec, (
    "add_record must return the created {{record}} as a dict including its new 'id'. "
    "Got %r." % (_rec,))
_rows = list_records(int(_uid))
assert isinstance(_rows, list) and len(_rows) == 1, (
    "list_records must return a list of the user's {{records}}. Got %r." % (_rows,))
assert isinstance(_rows[0], dict), (
    "list_records must return dicts, not row tuples - the page renders fields by name. "
    "Got %r." % (_rows[0],))
for _k in ("id", "{{title_field}}", "{{amount_field}}", "date"):
    assert _k in _rows[0], (
        "each {{record}} needs the key %r so the dashboard can render it. Got keys %r"
        % (_k, sorted(_rows[0])))
assert _rows[0]["{{title_field}}"] == "Sunrise loop", "list_records returned the wrong {{title_field}}."

_other = create_user("intruder@test.io", "x")
assert list_records(int(_other)) == [], (
    "list_records must only return the {{records}} belonging to the user id it is given. "
    "A second user could see the first user's data.")
assert delete_record(int(_rows[0]["id"]), int(_other)) in (False, 0, None), (
    "delete_record must not delete another user's {{record}}.")
assert list_records(int(_uid)) != [], (
    "delete_record deleted a {{record}} belonging to a different user - it is filtering on "
    "{{record}} id only. Filter on BOTH record_id and user_id.")

assert delete_record(int(_rows[0]["id"]), int(_uid)) in (True, 1), (
    "delete_record must return True when it deleted something, so the API can answer "
    "404 when it did not.")
assert list_records(int(_uid)) == [], "delete_record did not actually delete the {{record}}."
assert delete_record(9999, int(_uid)) in (False, 0), (
    "delete_record must return False for a {{record}} that does not exist.")

delete_session(_tok)
assert user_id_for_token(_tok) is None, (
    "delete_session must invalidate the token - logging out has to actually log out.")

pieces.name: pages
pieces.spec:
Write a module returning four complete HTML documents:
    landing_page(), signup_page(), login_page(), dashboard_page()

IMPORTANT - import the house UI kit and use it. Do NOT write your own CSS:
    from scaffold_partials import (page, field, button, link_button, message_slot,
                                   empty_state, card, auth_fetch_helper)

Build each page with page({{title_field}}, body, script=...). Build every input with
field(name, label, kind=..., autocomplete=...) so it is labelled. Use button() for actions and
message_slot() for errors.

signup_page and login_page post JSON to /api/signup and /api/login, store the returned token
with setToken(), then go to /dashboard.

dashboard_page loads GET /api/{{records}}, renders each with a Delete button, posts new ones to
POST /api/{{records}}, and deletes via DELETE /api/{{records}}/{id}. Include auth_fetch_helper() in
its script so the Authorization header is set for you.

When rendering a {{record}} you MUST pass its text through escapeHtml(), which is already defined
on every page. Writing user text into innerHTML unescaped is a stored cross-site-scripting
hole, and the checks will catch it.
pieces.tests:
# --- blueprint scenario: what the browser will actually be served ---------------
for _name, _fn in (("landing", landing_page), ("signup", signup_page),
                   ("login", login_page), ("dashboard", dashboard_page)):
    _html = _fn()
    assert isinstance(_html, str) and len(_html) > 200, (
        "%s_page() must return the full HTML document as a string. Got %r"
        % (_name, type(_html)))
    _low = _html.lower()
    assert "<!doctype html" in _low, (
        "%s_page() is missing its doctype - browsers fall into quirks mode without it."
        % _name)
    assert "viewport" in _low, (
        "%s_page() has no viewport meta tag, so it renders desktop-width on a phone."
        % _name)
    # The supplied page() helper inlines the kit, so the kit's own tokens are the proof
    # it was used. Do not write CSS by hand - build the page with scaffold_partials.page().
    assert "--tap" in _html and "--accent" in _html, (
        "%s_page() did not go through scaffold_partials.page(), so it is missing the "
        "house stylesheet. Import it and return page({{title_field}}, body) - the kit is what "
        "supplies focus rings, 44px tap targets and AA contrast." % _name)
    assert "undefined" not in _low, (
        "%s_page() contains a literal 'undefined' placeholder." % _name)

for _name, _fn in (("signup", signup_page), ("login", login_page)):
    _html = _fn().lower()
    assert _html.count("<label") >= 2, (
        "%s_page() needs a <label for=...> on every input. Use the supplied field() "
        "helper, which cannot emit an input without one." % _name)
    assert 'type="password"' in _html, (
        '%s_page() must use type="password" for the password field.' % _name)
    assert "autocomplete" in _html, (
        "%s_page() should set autocomplete on its fields so password managers work."
        % _name)

pieces.name: api
pieces.spec:
Write a FastAPI module defining `app` that imports the modules that already
exist:
    from passwords import hash_password, verify_password
    import storage
    import pages

Routes:
    GET    /api/health          -> {"status": "ok"}
    POST   /api/signup          -> 409 if the email exists, else 201 with {"token": ...}
    POST   /api/login           -> 401 on bad credentials, else {"token": ...}
    POST   /api/logout          -> {"ok": true}
    GET    /api/{{records}}         -> the caller's {{records}}
    POST   /api/{{records}}         -> creates one, 201
    DELETE /api/{{records}}/{id}    -> 404 if it is not the caller's
    GET    /, /signup, /login, /dashboard -> HTMLResponse(pages.<name>_page())

Use pydantic models for request bodies so malformed input returns 422, never 500.

AUTHENTICATION - this is the part that is easy to get wrong. Write your own function that
takes `request: Request`, reads the Authorization header, and resolves the bearer token with
storage.user_id_for_token, raising HTTPException(401) when it is absent or unknown. Then use
Depends(your_function).

Do NOT pass a storage function directly to Depends. FastAPI inspects the signature and would
treat its `token` parameter as a QUERY parameter, so anonymous callers get 422 instead of 401
and the auth check never runs.
pieces.tests:
# --- blueprint scenario: the API as a client actually meets it -----------------
# Driven through TestClient rather than by reading the source, because every failure
# this is guarding against looked correct in the source.
import glob as _glob
import os as _os

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient as _TestClient

# See the storage scenario: delete whatever database the module actually created, not a
# guessed list of names, or state survives between attempts and fails them for free.
for _f in _glob.glob("*.db") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite") + _glob.glob("*.sqlite3"):
    try:
        _os.remove(_f)
    except OSError:
        pass
import storage as _storage
_storage.init_db()

_c = _TestClient(app)

_r = _c.get("/api/health")
assert _r.status_code == 200, "GET /api/health must return 200, got %d" % _r.status_code
assert _r.json().get("status") == "ok", 'GET /api/health must return {"status": "ok"}'

# The failure that escalated this piece twice. Handing a storage function straight to
# Depends() makes FastAPI read its `token` parameter as a QUERY parameter, so an anonymous
# caller is told a query field is missing (422) and the auth check never runs at all.
_r = _c.get("/api/{{records}}")
assert _r.status_code == 401, (
    "an anonymous GET /api/{{records}} must return 401, got %d. If this is 422, a storage "
    "function was passed straight to Depends() - write your own dependency that takes "
    "`request: Request`, reads the Authorization header itself, and raises "
    "HTTPException(401)." % _r.status_code)

_r = _c.post("/api/signup", json={"email": "a@test.io", "password": "password-one"})
assert _r.status_code == 201, (
    "POST /api/signup must return 201 on success, got %d: %s"
    % (_r.status_code, _r.text[:200]))
_tok_a = _r.json().get("token")
assert isinstance(_tok_a, str) and _tok_a, "POST /api/signup must return {'token': ...}"

_r = _c.post("/api/signup", json={"email": "a@test.io", "password": "password-one"})
assert _r.status_code == 409, (
    "signing up with an email that already exists must return 409, got %d" % _r.status_code)

_r = _c.post("/api/login", json={"email": "a@test.io", "password": "wrong-password"})
assert _r.status_code == 401, (
    "POST /api/login with a bad password must return 401, got %d" % _r.status_code)
_r = _c.post("/api/login", json={"email": "a@test.io", "password": "password-one"})
assert _r.status_code == 200 and _r.json().get("token"), (
    "POST /api/login with correct credentials must return a token, got %d: %s"
    % (_r.status_code, _r.text[:200]))

_h_a = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + _tok_a}
_r = _c.post("/api/{{records}}", json={"{{title_field}}": "First", "{{amount_field}}": 12.5,
                                       "date": "2026-01-01"}, headers=_h_a)
assert _r.status_code == 201, (
    "POST /api/{{records}} must return 201, got %d: %s" % (_r.status_code, _r.text[:200]))

_r = _c.get("/api/{{records}}", headers=_h_a)
assert _r.status_code == 200, "GET /api/{{records}} must return 200 for a signed-in caller"
_rows = _r.json()
assert isinstance(_rows, list) and len(_rows) == 1, (
    "GET /api/{{records}} must return a list of the caller's {{records}}, got %r" % (_rows,))
assert _rows[0].get("{{title_field}}") == "First", (
    "each item needs its {{title_field}} so the page can render it, got %r" % (_rows[0],))
_rid = _rows[0].get("id")
assert _rid is not None, "each item needs an 'id' so it can be deleted, got %r" % (_rows[0],)

# A second account must be completely blind to the first.
_r = _c.post("/api/signup", json={"email": "b@test.io", "password": "password-two"})
_h_b = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + _r.json()["token"]}
assert _c.get("/api/{{records}}", headers=_h_b).json() == [], (
    "a new account can see another account's {{records}} - filter every query by the "
    "caller's user id.")
assert _c.delete("/api/{{records}}/%s" % _rid, headers=_h_b).status_code == 404, (
    "deleting another account's record must return 404, not delete it.")
assert len(_c.get("/api/{{records}}", headers=_h_a).json()) == 1, (
    "another account's DELETE actually removed the record.")

assert _c.get("/api/{{records}}", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer not-a-token"}
              ).status_code == 401, "an unknown bearer token must be refused with 401."

_r = _c.post("/api/{{records}}", json={"{{title_field}}": 5}, headers=_h_a)
assert _r.status_code == 422, (
    "a malformed body must return 422, got %d. Use a pydantic model for the request body "
    "so validation happens before your handler runs." % _r.status_code)

assert _c.delete("/api/{{records}}/%s" % _rid, headers=_h_a).status_code == 200, (
    "deleting your own record must succeed.")
assert _c.get("/api/{{records}}", headers=_h_a).json() == [], "the record was not deleted."
assert _c.delete("/api/{{records}}/%s" % _rid, headers=_h_a).status_code == 404, (
    "deleting a record that no longer exists must return 404.")

assert _c.post("/api/logout", headers=_h_a).status_code == 200, "POST /api/logout must work."
assert _c.get("/api/{{records}}", headers=_h_a).status_code == 401, (
    "the token still works after logout - /api/logout must delete the session.")

for _path in ("/", "/signup", "/login", "/dashboard"):
    _r = _c.get(_path)
    assert _r.status_code == 200, "GET %s must return 200, got %d" % (_path, _r.status_code)
    assert "text/html" in _r.headers.get("content-type", ""), (
        "GET %s must be served as HTML - return HTMLResponse(pages.<name>_page()), and "
        "declare response_class=HTMLResponse." % _path)
    assert "<!doctype html" in _r.text.lower(), (
        "GET %s did not return a full HTML document." % _path)

"""Entry point: wires the built pieces together and serves them."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

import storage
from api import app


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run the app.")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8099)
    ap.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    storage.init_db()
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host=args.host, port=args.port, log_level="warning")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
